# Bridge

The Hallam Street bridge is 40 metres long. It opened in March 1932 and cost the council £18,000. Trams crossed it until 1961.

The bridge stands as a lasting testament to the town's enduring spirit. Its legacy continues to shape the community in profound ways, marking a pivotal turning point in local history.

In 1998 a lorry hit the north rail, and the bridge was shut for six weeks. The repair used steel from the original supplier in Sheffield. This shows how much the town values its heritage.
